title: arxiv_2109.14306v1
universal_lens: A three-stream 3D/1D CNN framework fuses RGB, optical flow, and pose modalities for table tennis stroke classification and segmentation via bilinear feature fusion. Action discrimination through movement-derived features enables fine-grained sport analytics via sensor fusion and pose estimation.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference models the posterior probability of stroke classes given multi-modal video features, enabling conformal prediction of action labels with uncertainty quantification. Bayesian inference on athlete motion data integrates body-worn sensor streams to classify actions with conformal uncertainty quantification.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning maps temporal action segments to state transitions in player performance, supporting real-time feedback generation through dynamic pose and motion flow analysis. Situational reasoning maps real-time pose and sensor states into dynamic action state transitions using probabilistic temporal logic.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 4 explores the synthesis of 3D skeletal pose and depth information from monocular inputs to enhance motion analysis in sports. The core innovation lies in fusing pose estimation with depth computation to generate holistic 3D models of athlete movements. This approach leverages pose vectors derived from 2D image analysis and supplements them with depth estimates obtained via single-image techniques. The resulting 3D skeletons enable richer feedback mechanisms for stroke and gesture evaluation. The paper emphasizes that such fusion improves classification accuracy by up to 18% when integrated with RGB and optical flow streams. Temporal coherence in pose estimation is critical for robustness, suggesting future work should incorporate temporal convolutional layers to refine joint tracking. The implications extend to performance assessment, where deviations from baseline motion patterns can be quantified. The study also highlights limitations in current datasets like TTStroke-21, which lack qualitative annotations—pointing towards expert-driven quality assessments as a next frontier. From a foundational standpoint, this chapter establishes a mathematical framework for multimodal motion understanding, bridging perception and cognition in athletic analytics.
